newsitem.title: USA: BPA CUTS FIRM, PEAK POWER FOR MONDAY $6-7 PER MWH.
newsitem.headline: BPA CUTS FIRM, PEAK POWER FOR MONDAY $6-7 PER MWH.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Friday it cut its offer of firm, peak electricity for Monday by $6.00-7.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).

The Portland, Oregon-based federal agency offered 400 megawatts (MW) of firm, peak electricity for Monday delivery at $18.00 a MWh for Northwest delivery and $20.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) delivery.
BPA offered non-firm power for Monday at $17.00 a MWh for hours 0800-1100 PDT for Northwest delivery and $19.00 for COB delivery.
The agency offered Monday non-firm power for 1200-2200 EDT at $20.00 to the Northwest and $22.00 at COB.
For Monday, BPA offered to sell off-peak, non-firm power for Northwest delivery at $13.00-15.00 and for COB delivery at $15.00-17.00.
For Saturday and Sunday, BPA offered peak, firm power for Northwest delivery at $16.00-16.50 and for COB delivery at $18.00-18.50.
The agency offered to sell firm, off-peak power for Saturday and Sunday for Northwest delivery at $12.00 and for COB delivery at $14.00 per MWh.

For Saturday, BPA offered to sell non-firm power for the hours of 0100-0700 and 2300-2400 PDT for Northwest delivery at $12.00 and COB delivery at $14.00, for 0800-1200 PDT Northwest delivery was offered at $14.00 and COB delivery at $16.00, and 1300-2200 PDT for Northwest delivery at $18.00 and COB at $20.00.

For Sunday, BPA offered to sell non-firm power for the hours of 0100-0800, 2300-2400 PDT for Northwest delivery at $12.00 and COB delivery $14.00. F 0900-1300 PDT, Northwest delivery was offered at $14.00 and COB delivery $16.00, and for the hours of 1400-2200 PDT, Northwest delivery was offered at $17.00 and COB delivery at $19.00.
